title: Ridership Demand Considerations in New Fare Adjustment Formula
what_it_is: Ridership Demand Considerations in New Fare Adjustment Formula

sections.label: PTC fare formula recommendations
sections.summary: The PTC released recommendations on fare adjustment formula and mechanism changes, to be applied from this year's Fare Review Exercise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The Public Transport Council (PTC) has released its recommendations on changes to the fare adjustment formula and mechanism to reduce volatility of fare adjustments, while ensuring fare affordability for commuters and the financial sustainability of the public transport system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The new fare formula will be applied from this year's Fare Review Exercise, which will be carried out in the later part of this year.

sections.label: Fixed C at 1.1%
sections.summary: To reduce variability, the PTC proposed "C", fixed for the next five years at 1.1%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: To reduce this variability, the PTC proposed "C", which is fixed for the next five years at 1.1%.

sections.label: Government fare affordability commitment
sections.summary: The Government remains committed to keeping fares affordable, subsidising public transport operations at more than $2 billion yearly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Whatever the formula, the Government remains committed to keeping fares affordable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: And that is why on top of fully funding the public transport infrastructure, we subsidise public transport operations at more than $2 billion every year or, as I have said just yesterday, more than $1 for every public transport journey.

sections.label: Bus and train subsidies
sections.summary: The Government provides about a billion dollars each for buses and trains, and deferred fare increases add to subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The first and at the systemic level is what we do for buses and trains.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And I have said this before, today we provide about a billion dollars each for buses and trains by way of subsidy from the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I would add that any fare increase that is not implemented is also rolled over and that adds to the subsidy and/or the support that is accorded public transport from the Government, the public purse.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, because we deferred a significant portion of the fare increase last year, we now have another $200 million of subsidies – a fare deferral consequence.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Whether it is concession fares, where there is the normal adult fare, and then those who hold concession cards can pay at a reduced rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And also, there are the cards that you buy per month, the season passes if you like, which as I have explained, for example, it is at $64 	for senior citizens at this point, which is approximately $2 a day for unlimited travel.

sections.label: Scope to enhance support
sections.summary: On whether support can be increased or enhanced, the speaker says that is an area being worked on across all three levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: To the Member's question on whether there is scope to increase or enhance the support that is accorded, I think that is an area that we continue to work on across all three levels.

sections.label: Ridership recovery from pandemic
sections.summary: Public transport ridership is about 90% of the pre-pandemic level, with a variegated outcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I do not have a precise number, but I think ex ante, as I have said, our public transport ridership is still recovering from the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We are now about 90% of the pre-pandemic level and it also is a quite variegated outcome.

sections.label: PTV take-up rates
sections.summary: The speaker says PTV take-up is significant, with more than half of the 600,000 provided taken up.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Our take-up rates, I know that they are quite significant.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We were quite generous in providing for PTVs in the last round – 600,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And the reason was because of the combination of both the fare increase and the economic circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: It is not fully taken up, but I know that more than half, or quite a significant proportion, has been taken up, or in that order of magnitude.
